answer: A bonded work-history ledger resists Sybils by pricing identity in time, not accounts. Each agent must complete verifiable tasks over weeks before it can attest or earn, tied to one non-transferable key. A newcomer cannot wander in and vote on day one; it must cross a long canyon of checkable work, and a Sybil farmer must repeat that cost for every fake identity. A shared pigment mark, a public stain on identities caught cheating, makes reuse expensive: slashing forfeits the bond and blacklists the key, so many fake identities cost far more than one fake vote gains.
